Experimental variability is concentrated in a minority of repeat-measured compounds

Estradiol, 1Source for 1Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv-butanol, and caffeine have selected-subset experimental ranges above 1.0Source for 1.0Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv log10 unit; methotrexate reaches exactly 1.000Source for 1.000Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv. For the 54Source for 54Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv repeated compounds, the median range is 0.381Source for 0.381Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv and 22Source for 22Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv receive an identical LGBM prediction across all their selected rows. Even the largest prediction range is below 0.1Source for 0.1Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv. This gap indicates limited representation of row-specific experimental context, not proof that any one condition caused the observed differences.

Protocol signatures are completely coupled to literature sources

The citations span 1964–2012. Coverage is not dominated by one paper: the top five references contribute 22.3%Source for 22.3%Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv of rows and the top ten contribute 35.9%Source for 35.9%Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv. However, all 140Source for 140Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv recorded condition signatures occur within only one reference. Consequently, reference/laboratory effects and protocol effects cannot be separated using simple grouped comparisons in this selected subset.

Same-reference pH series are the clearest condition-linked examples

Scope, data, and definitions

One row is one reported measurement. Compounds are grouped by canonical SMILES. The cohort includes only rows with absolute LGBM prediction error ≤0.6Source for 0.6Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv. Experimental variability is max minus min logKp within a compound; fold range is 10Source for 10Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv raised to that difference. Unknown, empty, N/A, and not-reported values count as unavailable. A condition context combines all 14Source for 14Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv condition fields with reference and DOI.

Methodology

The analysis profiles completeness, citation concentration, repeated-measurement counts, within-compound experimental and prediction ranges, condition-signature uniqueness, and repeated series within a citation. It preserves every source measurement and adds annotations rather than averaging measurements. Exact row counts, calculations, and charts are reproducible in the companion notebook.

Limitations and robustness checks

This subset is selected using experimental logKp, creating outcome-dependent selection bias; it is not an unbiased validation cohort. Most compounds have only one selected measurement. Conditions are incompletely reported, several fields co-vary, and condition signatures are nested within references. The pH associations are descriptive, not causal. Row count, source-row uniqueness, the inclusive ±0.6Source for 0.6Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv rule, 171Source for 171Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv-compound count, 71Source for 71Source: HuSkinDB LGBM ±0.6 selected measurement tableTable: lgbm_within_0.6_selected_measurement_conditions.csv-reference count, and notebook execution were verified.

Recommended next steps

  1. Fit any condition-effect analysis on the full, unfiltered HuSkinDB table, not this outcome-selected subset.
  2. Use a hierarchical model with compound and reference effects before estimating pH, temperature, layer, preparation, donor/acceptor medium, or cell-type associations.
  3. Add ionization/pH and other protocol variables to future prediction models; the current LGBM condition input is limited to experimental temperature (Texpi).
  4. Treat single-measurement compounds as variability unknown, not variability low.

Further questions

Can the original papers resolve the high missingness in storage duration and pH? Are units and skin-thickness conventions harmonized across references? Does a full-dataset multilevel model retain the pH patterns after controlling for compound, reference, skin layer, preparation, and medium?
